text.p: Greenpeace activists said on Wednesday thay had seized the tiny and barren Atlantic island of Rockall to protest over oil exploration.
Three environmentalists from Britain, Australia and Germany were airlifted by helicopter on to the island and set up their base in a solar survival capsule screwed by steel pins into a rocky ledge.
"The seas around Rockall, potentially rich in oil, are fought over by four nations -- Britain, Denmark, Iceland and Ireland," said one of the activists whose name was given as Al.
"By seizing Rockall, we claim her seas for the planet and all its people. No one has the right to unleash this oil on to our threatened climate," he said in a statement put out by Greenpeace.
Greenpeace campaign director Chris Rose said; "Science shows the climate cannot survive the burning of the oil we have already got.
"It is an insane and hypocritical policy to look for more. Greenpeace disputes the moral and political right of the UK to develop this ocean for more oil."

Rockall is situated about 300 miles from the Scotttish mainland and Greenpeace said its activists would be using their capsule as a "campaign base for monitoring and communicating the expansion of oil fields into the Atlantic Frontier."
Eleven exploration licences covering 58 full and partial blocks in the Rockall Trough, where water depths exceed 1,500 metres, were awarded on June 4 by the Department of Energy in Dublin.
